title: Biosynthesized jujube mediated trimetallic (Ag–Zn–Mn) nanoparticles supported on graphene oxide: new tyrosinase inhibitors with environmental remediation applications
content: A novel green and eco-friendly procedure for the synthesis of Ziziphus mauritiana Lam. based trimetallic silver-zinc-manganese supported on graphene oxide (ZML-AZM@GO) nanoparticles (NPs) has been developed. The study focuses on the successful use of the stem extract of ZML as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. The synthesis of the NPs has been confirmed with the help of various analytical techniques like UV-vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, EDX, TGA, and SEM analysis. These techniques successfully revealed that a homogeneous combination of crystallite Ag, ZnO, and MnO, NPs has been produced over the partly exfoliated structure of GO. TGA illustrated improved thermal stability whereas SEM images showed that the amount of GO makes the nano-sheets uniform porous structures with less aggregation. The ZML-AZM@GO, NPs illustrated satisfactory catalytic activity in the reduction of risky nitro-aromatic pollutants like 2-nitrophenol, 4-nitrophenol, 4-nitroaniline, picric acid, and 2,4-dinitrophenyhydrazone, showing reduction effectiveness of around 99 percent within just a few minutes after the addition of NaBH4. Also, the NPs exhibited excellent catalytic action during the breakdown of many organic dyes like methylene blue, methyl orange, rhodamine B, crystal violet, brilliant green, eosin Y, and indigo carmine, showing degradation efficiency ranged from (97–98) percent. The NPs were shown to work efficiently against a mixture of organic pollutants. Also, besides its catalytic property, the biosynthesized NPs have shown a remarkable in vitro inhibitory effect against both human and fungal tyrosinase with no toxicity, confirming its applicable biopharmaceutical properties. High multifunctional activity is displayed with the contribution of effective linking of Ag–Zn–Mn-NPs with high surface area and excellent electrical conductivity of GO and active phytochemicals present in Z. mauritian. To summarize the findings, the study presents a new environmentally friendly approach in producing a unique multi-purpose material which may be applied in wastewater treatment, environmental remediation, and tyrosinase inhibition.
